blocks.heading: System contract and scope
text: Cumulus is the managed IoT control plane. This HLD covers the operator command path and OTA firmware rollouts, which together account for nearly all current production traffic; telemetry ingest is explicitly out of scope.
Both flows preserve the same state contract: the platform is authoritative for desired state in Registry, while each device is authoritative for its reported state.
bullets: Every state change passes through the versioned device-shadow Registry
Cloud-to-device transport is MQTT over TLS on port 8883 through Relay
Devices accept no inbound connections; they initiate all subscribe and publish activity
Site-prefixed topics separate cmd, ack, and out-of-scope telemetry traffic per device
Site 4 examples span a sleepy Thermostat T-100, always-connected Pump P-7, and a Modbus-bridging Edge Gateway
Document status: Draft 4; owned by platform-core; last updated 2026-08-19

sections.heading: Operator command loop
text: An operator changes Pump P-7's target flow rate. Authorization, versioned desired-state persistence, QoS 1 delivery, and the device's reported-state acknowledgment form one closed loop back to the Console.
Sentinel verifies both JWT signature and device.write scope before Dispatch sees the request; only site-operator and platform-admin roles receive that scope.
bullets: Failed scope checks return 403 at Nimbus and never reach Dispatch
Dispatch validates against reported capabilities before writing desired state
Stale shadow versions are retryable conflicts surfaced to the Console
The command uses QoS 1 with retain off on cmd/site-4/pump-7
Relay fans out to Pump P-7 and the Edge Gateway production subscriber for site supervisory control; Thermostat T-100 receives nothing
Broker PUBACK and the application ack are distinct; only the latter carries new reported state

contract.title: On the wire: command publish (MQTT)

fields.g: the target state document written to Registry
shadow version the write was based on; stale versions are retryable conflicts
carried from Console through acknowledgment for end-to-end tracing
at-least-once delivery; devices dedup on version

contract.note: The application ack on ack/site-4/pump-7 echoes version and trace_id; the broker PUBACK carries neither.

steps.text: The Console submits the command with the operator's bearer token.
Sentinel verifies the JWT signature and device.write scope before routing continues.
If Sentinel rejects the token, Nimbus returns 403 to the Console and nothing reaches Dispatch.
Nimbus forwards only the authorized command to Dispatch.
Dispatch validates capabilities and writes versioned desired state.
Dispatch publishes the non-retained command at QoS 1.
Relay delivers to Pump P-7 and the Edge Gateway production subscriber for site supervisory control.
Pump P-7 confirms broker delivery with PUBACK.
After execution, Pump P-7 publishes reported state on its application ack topic.
Dispatch consumes the application acknowledgment.
Dispatch records the device's new reported state in Registry.
The Console subscription observes the update and closes the operator loop.

sections.heading: Sleepy-device delivery
text: Thermostat T-100 normally sleeps with its radio off. Relay retains its QoS 1 command in a persistent session and delivers it in the next firmware-controlled wake window rather than losing it.
This makes sleepy-device commands eventually consistent by design: desired state is already authoritative while reported state remains behind.
bullets: Battery-class devices use clean_session=false
T-100 currently wakes every 15 minutes
The Console shows pending delivery until the application acknowledgment arrives
Sleepy devices are excluded from command-latency SLOs
Open TODO: document the per-session queue depth at which Relay begins dropping messages

steps.text: Dispatch publishes after desired state is versioned; the Console shows pending delivery.
Relay queues the QoS 1 message while the radio sleeps, then delivers it at the next wake window.
T-100 executes the command and publishes its reported state.
Relay returns the application acknowledgment to Dispatch.
Dispatch advances the reported shadow document.
The Console replaces pending delivery with the applied state.

sections.heading: Canary-to-fleet stage gates
text: OTA reuses the command transport, but Dispatch's rollout coordinator drives the flow rather than an operator click. The prose-defined stages are normative even though the HLD contains no sequence diagram for them.
A release engineer first registers the image digest, target hardware revision, and minimum battery level in Registry; Dispatch then opens the canary stage.
bullets: The pilot canary cohort is Edge Gateway plus one device per hardware class
Every canary must report the new version inside the stage window before fleet rollout begins
Fleet offers are issued in batches of 50 with a 10-minute soak between batches
A failed or silent canary freezes the rollout and pages the release engineer
There is no automatic rollback because reverting flashed firmware is itself another rollout

steps.text: The release engineer registers digest, hardware target, and minimum battery level.
Dispatch opens the rollout in canary stage and selects the policy-defined cohort.
Dispatch publishes one QoS 1 update offer per canary command topic.
Relay delivers offers to Edge Gateway and one device from every hardware class.
Only a complete set of in-window canary version reports opens fleet stage.
Dispatch offers the update to the next batch of 50 devices.
The coordinator holds a 10-minute soak before evaluating the next batch.
Passing batches repeat until no eligible devices remain.
The rollout completes after the final batch reports the new version.
A failed or silent stage freezes progress and pages the release engineer; rollback is manual.

sections.heading: Per-device OTA install
text: An OTA offer is only control-plane metadata. The selected device retrieves firmware directly from the artifact store over HTTPS; Relay never carries image bytes.
After validating the digest, the device flashes, reboots, and publishes its installed version on the normal ack topic so Dispatch can evaluate the stage gate.
bullets: Offer delivery and the version report use the existing per-device MQTT command and ack topics
The device must verify the registered digest before flashing
The broker transports offers and reports, never the firmware binary

steps.text: Dispatch publishes an OTA offer, not image bytes, at QoS 1.
Relay delivers the offer through the device's existing command topic.
The device downloads the firmware image directly from the artifact store over HTTPS.
The device verifies the registered digest before it writes firmware.
A verified image is flashed and activated by rebooting the device.
The rebooted device publishes its installed version on the ack topic.
Dispatch consumes the version report and evaluates whether the stage may advance.

sections.heading: Failure taxonomy and retry ladder
text: Failures are classified where first observed. Only delivery, acknowledgment, and OTA-offer failures enter the shared exponential-backoff ladder.

From the operator's perspective delivery and ack timeouts behave identically. Ack timeouts usually indicate firmware failure after successful delivery, but reliably distinguishing the two cases from broker session state remains an open item.
bullets: Sentinel auth failures are terminal, never retried, and surface as 401/403
Dispatch capability-validation failures are synchronous and include a machine-readable reason
Registry version conflicts are caller-retryable; Console refreshes and retries once before showing an error
Timeout backoff is 1, 4, then 16 minutes
After the third failed OTA attempt, the device is dead-lettered, excluded from remaining stages, and shown with its last error
After the third failed operator command attempt, it is marked undeliverable and desired/reported divergence is flagged
Edge Gateway's cmd/site-4/# log is the first artifact pulled for delivery disputes

steps.text: A delivery, acknowledgment, or OTA-offer timeout enters the shared retry policy.
Dispatch retries after one minute.
A repeated failure schedules the four-minute backoff.
Dispatch makes the second retry after four minutes.
Another failure schedules the final 16-minute backoff.
Dispatch makes the third and final retry.
The terminal state depends on whether the failed work was OTA or an operator command.
Console exposes the last OTA error or flags desired/reported divergence for commands.

sections.heading: Operational commitments
text: The production envelope is defined by observed line-powered-device latency, intentionally overprovisioned broker capacity, short-lived operator credentials, end-to-end tracing, and site-prefixed topics.
bullets: Site 4 command-to-PUBACK latency is p50 180 ms and p99 900 ms for line-powered devices
Relay supports 10,000 concurrent sessions per node; site 4 currently uses three
Cloud services use mutual TLS; devices use per-device X.509 certificates rotated annually
Sentinel JWTs expire after 15 minutes and the Console refreshes them silently
Every command carries trace_id from Console through acknowledgment
Dispatch emits one span for every rollout stage transition
The site-prefixed topic layout is multi-site-ready; only the examples are site-4-specific
